analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. It bumps the last-updated date (line 3) and adds a description around line 1293 of PromptPieceTokenStore.lookup behavior: hits are snapshotted before promotion between two bounded generations, so a rotation mid-lookup cannot turn a later piece into a miss. The text states that token arrays share storage during the snapshot, that existing admission and byte bounds still apply, and that batches with no old-generation hits skip the promotion pass. I reviewed the two supplied head units (lines 1612-2426 of the doc), which are unchanged context. They cover MTP upgrade, sampling, constrained JSON, tool parsers, vision and MiMo, and none are altered by the patch. No code, config, endpoint, key handling or trust-boundary change is visible. The described cache is scoped to the prefix-cache scope, which is consistent with T-041's coordinator-authored cacheSalt scoping, and the doc says per-scope reuse is unchanged. Remaining integration question: the actual PromptPieceTokenStore Swift change is not in the supplied evidence. If it ships in the same PR, reviewers should confirm that scope keys still partition the piece-token cache, that no cross-scope hits are exposed, and that bounds hold (T-041 timing and cross-tenant oracle, T-028). This doc-only diff gives no evidence of a regression, and the T-041 threat model does not need updating from it.
